gaps.topic: Diagnostic-boot safety envelope and attribution: the watcher kill rules and the D12 auto-mode proof do not match the observed failure dynamics
gaps.why_it_matters: The plan's #1 item is the first nvidia boot. Its kill rule (MemAvailable <1.5 GiB for 5 s, or PSI full avg10 >20%) is slower than the recorded collapse. Stock proof: 13.82 GiB at 00:46:51, 10.33 at :54, 0.59 at :58. batch1024: 17.70 to 6.39 in 4 s. That is about 2.5-3.4 GiB/s at a 3-4 s watcher cadence, and stop.sh then needed 11-20 s to clear the containers. This is the same failure class as the 2026-08-31 spark2 global OOM (CONSTRAINT_NONE, NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY). conduit and L.A.I.L also run on spark1. The census also has blind spots. TileLang's mHC compile finishes seconds before every collapse, so a regex 'nvcc|cicc|cudafe++|ninja|ptxas' fires on the wrong JIT. FlashInferB12xNvFp4LinearKernel compiles CuTe-DSL in-process, so no compiler process appears at all, and the plan's own open question 1 says auto may pick b12x. Two cheaper signals go unused. First, the kernel choice is logged at construction ('Using %s for NVFP4 GEMM', info_once, emitted from ModelOptNvFp4LinearMethod.__init__ at modelopt.py:1104-1107 and kernels/linear/__init__.py:1073). That line appears about 13 minutes before the dangerous phase, so a boot can be classified and aborted early. Second, FlashInfer JIT writes 'flashinfer.jit:' lines into the engine log (rebench engine-rank1.log.tail:68-71).

gaps.topic: Boot time and host memory policy are unplanned prerequisites for a ~60 slot-hour, boot-bound programme
gaps.why_it_matters: Every experiment is ABAB at 2 boots per arm, and each boot takes about 18 minutes. The head node loads in 629-785 s against 190-240 s on the worker, and each rank streams the full 190.40 GiB checkpoint. That includes 13.84 GiB of unused BF16 layer 45: at about 0.26 GiB/s on the head, that layer alone costs about 50 s, not 30 s. So boots take a large share of the 58-63 slot-hours, yet the plan has no lever for boot time; it lists this only as open question 8. Separately, spark1 currently runs vm.swappiness=60 with a 16 GiB swapfile (3.5 GiB in use). Tony's GB10 notes (tony_readme.md:246-250, 375-377) call swappiness=0 mandatory: at the default, the kernel pages vLLM out mid-load and a UVM livelock follows. The nvidia proof also recorded swap rising from 151 MiB to 1.6 GiB at abort. The plan defers swappiness to P4, the last phase, and proposes 1 rather than 0. That leaves a boot-safety and variance variable uncontrolled across the calibration, the diagnostic and every receipt.

gaps.topic: Statistical feasibility of the plan's gates: the nvidia-flip non-inferiority margin, the Tier-1 pass rule and ruler-v2 step counting
gaps.why_it_matters: The flip criterion says 'Ruler v2 on the same session: step_ms non-inferior by at most +2%'. Two packs cannot share a session, and the plan's own §6 puts the MDE at 6-10% with 2 boots per arm, at a boot CV of 2.2-3.7%. So the criterion is untestable as written: it will either block the default flip indefinitely or be waived. Tier 1 requires 'no McNemar p<0.05 regression and a paired lower bound >= -5pp' on each task. At MMMU n=60 with about 20% discordance, the 95% half-width is about 11pp. So identical packs fail, and 8-10 tests at alpha 0.05 give a false-fail rate of roughly 20-35%. Ruler v2 also counts steps from ITL, but the verifier validated that only 'when async scheduling is off', while SYS-11 confirms async scheduling is on for DFlash. Forced-length 512-token cells (EOS banned) may bias acceptance. These gates decide the user's headline request (the nvidia default) and every keep or revert.

errors_in_plan: Kill rule is slower than the observed collapse. 'Kill on MemAvailable below 1.5 GiB for 5 s, PSI full avg10 >20%' cannot fire in time. Recorded descent: 13.82 GiB (00:46:51) to 10.33 (:54) to 0.59 (:58) in glm53-nvidia-spark-proof.md:37-38,75-76; 17.70 to 6.39/4.37 GiB in 4 s in glm53-nvidia-batch1024-proof.md:51-52. That is about 2.5-3.4 GiB/s. Stop latency was 11-20 s (abort 00:46:58, containers gone 00:47:09; batch1024 abort 02:29:45, free at 02:30:05). The same failure class produced a global OOM on spark2 on 2026-08-31 (evidence/oom-20260831/diagnosis.txt: CONSTRAINT_NONE global_oom, NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY). The trigger needs a floor above rate × (sample interval + kill latency), plus a slope rule and a parallel SIGKILL of both ranks.

The D12 auto-mode proof ('kill at the first compiler process', census 'nvcc|cicc|cudafe++|ninja|ptxas') is unsafe and can mis-attribute. (a) TileLang's mHC JIT finishes seconds before every collapse (all six proofs), so it trips a generic compiler census before the dense MLP runs. (b) If auto picks FlashInferB12xNvFp4LinearKernel, the plan's open question 1, the CuTe-DSL compile happens in-process (kernels/linear/nvfp4/flashinfer.py:308-360). No compiler process appears, and the boot runs unguarded. A cheaper signal already exists: 'Using %s for NVFP4 GEMM' is logged at construction, because ModelOptNvFp4LinearMethod.__init__ calls init_nvfp4_linear_kernel (modelopt.py:1104-1107; __init__.py:1073, info_once scope 'local'). A boot can therefore be classified, and aborted, about 13 minutes before the profile forward. FlashInfer JIT also logs 'flashinfer.jit:' lines into the engine log (rebench engine-rank1.log.tail:68-71).

'The four one-knob variants (eager, batch1024, language-only, skip-mm) rule out CUDA graphs, activation size, the vision tower and the multimodal dummy' is wrong in two ways. First, the variants were stacked, not one knob off stock: skip-mm included video:0, and batch1024 was skip-mm plus 1024 (batch1024-proof.md:12,107-116). Second, profile_run happens before graph capture, and Glm5Next forces CompilationMode.NONE (b12x-B engine log: 'mode': CompilationMode.NONE), so eager changes nothing in the failing phase. What the variants show is that no single factor is sufficient to prevent the drop. Contribution is not ruled out: the stock video:1 run dropped deepest (0.59/0.45) against 6.46/9.77 with skip-mm.

'From about 19 GiB to 0.45-10.4 GiB in 3-7 s' misreads the data. 0.45-10.4 are the watcher's kill-sample values (the first sample below 8 GiB on either node), not troughs (sibling-recipes.md:126,456). The fall from about 19-20 GiB took 10-32 s. In the stock run there was a plateau near 14 GiB during the encoder profile, and only the final 13.8→0.59 GiB took 7 s. The Phase 0.2 replay fixture '19.3 → 0.59 in 7 s' is wrong for the same reason: it should be 13.82→10.33→0.59 over 00:46:51-:58.

The 'Confound [C]: an 8 GiB watcher would also kill the published config' is overstated as an argument against the JIT hypothesis. LibertAI reaches 5.0-5.7 GiB only after KV (4.14 GiB) and graphs are allocated. The nvidia boots fell below 8 GiB during profile_run, before KV allocation (proofs: 'KV pin never logged'). At that phase LibertAI's MemAvailable was never logged at 1 s resolution; the '~11 GiB' in the healthy curve is arithmetic, not a measurement (open-prs.md:14,28). So nvidia is deeper at the same phase, and ladder rung 2 ('watcher artifacts') is the least likely outcome.

The EXTRA_ENV allowlist '^(NCCL|VLLM|TORCH|OMP|CUDA|MAX_JOBS)_' rejects the variables the plan needs. MAX_JOBS has no trailing underscore, so it does not match. FLASHINFER_* (cache and workspace dirs), PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF, TRITON_* and TILELANG_* are also rejected. The anchored 'TORCH_' does not match 'PYTORCH_'. Ladder rung 1 (MAX_JOBS=2, persistent JIT caches) therefore cannot go through it.

The flip criterion 'Ruler v2 on the same session: step_ms non-inferior by at most +2%' is impossible and untestable. Each pack is its own boot, so the two packs never share a session. Boot-level step CV is 2.2-3.7%, and the plan's own §6 puts the MDE at 6-10% with 2 boots per arm (verifier, regression-bench.md:374-378). A +2% margin needs many more boots per arm, or a margin consistent with the MDE.

The Tier-1 pass rule is underpowered and suffers from multiplicity. 'No McNemar p<0.05 regression and paired lower bound >= -5pp' per task at n=60 (MMMU), 120 (BFCL) and 150 (IFEval): at MMMU n=60 with about 20% discordance, the paired 95% half-width is about ±11pp, so identical packs fail the -5pp bound. Eight to ten separate tests at alpha 0.05 add roughly a 20-35% false-fail rate. The rule needs pooling or correction, or larger n.

The v12 'Python-only' layer (0.8) bundles router fp32, the Glm5Next mHC warmup, the prefix-cache draft-group fix and the layer-45 skip. Only the indexer factor is described as env-gated. If the Phase-1 calibration and diagnostic boots run on v12 (built 'at the start of slot 1'), they change routing numerics and TTFT behaviour relative to every v11 receipt at once. That breaks AGENTS.md's one-knob rule and pre-empts P3.e (router fp32 is itself a Phase-3 knob). Every patch must default to off, verified by v11-vs-v12 greedy byte-identity, or Phase 1 must run on v11.

Host VM policy is ordered too late. spark1 runs vm.swappiness=60 with a 16 GiB swapfile (/proc/sys/vm/swappiness; SwapFree 13.1 of 16 GiB now). Tony's GB10 guidance says swappiness=0 is mandatory, because at the default the kernel pages vLLM out mid-load and a UVM livelock follows (tony_readme.md:246-250,375-377). The nvidia proof recorded swap rising from 151 MiB to 1.6 GiB at abort (spark-proof.md:92). The plan leaves this to P4 (last phase), proposes 1 rather than 0, and omits it from the fallback ladder. D9 has to be decided before the Phase-1 boots and held constant, with a restore step when the nodes are handed back to DeepSeek.

ncu in Phase 1 step 8 will fail as specified. The host has RmProfilingAdminOnly: 1 (/proc/driver/nvidia/params), and nothing in the plan grants CAP_SYS_ADMIN (run.sh's docker run adds only IPC_LOCK). The microbench container needs --cap-add SYS_ADMIN, which needs owner OK. nsys GPU metrics have the same restriction; plain CUDA tracing does not. Whether nsys and ncu are present in the image is also unchecked.

Layer-45 skip 'about 30 s of boot' is understated. The head is the critical path at about 0.26 GiB/s (190.40 GiB in 733 s), so 13.84 GiB of skipped reads saves about 50 s. That matches the plan's own '+32 s' for the +9.1 GiB delta.

'About 73% of the drop comes from the ruler' overstates precision. The verifier's corrected claim is 'roughly 60-75%', with 4-6 ms/step of the step-time rise at DF5 unattributed (regression-bench.md FOR-1, lines 34-38).

'The largest quality lever is the pack switch itself' contradicts confirmed QUAL-4. On Marlin, the nvidia pack's calibrated W4A4 scales are unused; the verifier's corrected impact is 'unmeasured; treat PR #11 as a provenance change until a paired Tier-0 NLL comparison exists' (quality.md:139-141). The up_proj mis-scale mechanism is real: the published LibertAI logs contain 'w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2' (rebench engine.log.tail, engine-rank1.log.tail; modelopt.py:1530-1538). The nvidia pack has 0/12096 mismatches and tied dense scales (re-verified). But the size of the effect is unknown, so this should read 'largest candidate quality lever, possibly zero'.

Fallback rung 4 (SKIP_MM_PROFILING) has already been tested and failed (skipmm-proof: died at 6.46/9.77 GiB). It breaks AGENTS.md ('do not skip MM profiling'). It only adds information if combined with the pinned Marlin backend, so it should be dropped or reframed.

P4 keeps 'dual rail (TTFT −3-6%)' although the appendix discards dual rail. The −3-6% rests on SYS-7's comm share, which used the logger's 4438 tok/s window average rather than the measured 1443 tok/s needle prefill (system-uma-comm MISSED-3), so it is overstated by about 3x. Dual rail also means changing the pinned NCCL_IB_HCA, and AGENTS.md notes that two of the four HCAs are DOWN.

The pack for Phase 2+ is unspecified. Drafter and k decisions depend on acceptance, and acceptance doubles as a quant-fidelity metric (SD-9). They must run on the pack chosen at the end of Phase 1; otherwise results measured on LibertAI will not transfer after the nvidia flip.

The per-decision budget (~1.6 h: 4 boots × 18 min + fast gates) leaves out Tier 0 (15-20 min), which the plan requires 'for every performance knob'. With Tier 0 per arm, a decision costs about 2.2 h, so the Phase 2-3 budget is understated by about 35%.

Co-tenant handling is incomplete. 0.10 (drafter downloads to both nodes while DeepSeek serves) has no owner-OK gate, unlike 0.8 and 0.11. There is also no hand-back gate after each slot: MemAvailable back to about 117 GiB, no leftover containers, sysctl and swap restored, and DeepSeek health verified.
